business_problem: Yousician needed to stop spending engineering time maintaining a six-shard self-managed MongoDB environment and move to a more automated platform that could keep pace with product growth and user spikes.
solution_summary: Yousician migrated from a self-managed MongoDB deployment to MongoDB Atlas so its music-learning services could scale without the ongoing overhead of cluster maintenance. MongoDB consultants helped the team simulate the migration, then move development, staging, and production in sequence before pointing the applications at the new Atlas cluster. Atlas became the operational platform for Yousician and GuitarTuna, automating backups, upgrades, and cluster management while preserving the flexible document model the company already relied on. Yousician later added Atlas Search to GuitarTuna so users could search thousands of artists, songs, chords, and lyrics without operating separate search infrastructure. The result is a managed application data platform that supports millions of additional users, faster cluster provisioning, and better reliability during demand spikes such as the surge in at-home music learning during the pandemic.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs the core application data platform for Yousician and GuitarTuna while automating backups, upgrades, and scaling.

solution_components.name: Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Powers song, chord, lyric, and artist search experiences inside GuitarTuna without separate search infrastructure.

data_flow: User activity, lesson metadata, and application state are stored in MongoDB Atlas, Atlas Search indexes music content for fast relevance-based retrieval, and the applications return personalized search and learning experiences to mobile users in real time.
business_outcome: Yousician reduced maintenance work, improved availability, provisioned new clusters in minutes instead of days, and handled millions of additional users without disrupting the experience for music learners.
metrics: Yousician and GuitarTuna have a combined 20 million monthly active users.
The catalog includes 3,800 songs and over 9,000 lessons.
The self-managed cluster consisted of six shards.
The platform handles 3,000 requests per second and new clusters can be spun up in ten minutes.
architecture_clues: The migration followed a development, staging, and production sequence after a simulation run.
Atlas automates backups and version upgrades that were previously handled manually.
Atlas Search is used to query artists, songs, chords, and lyrics for GuitarTuna.

“Then, applications simply had to be pointed towards Atlas and the new platform was up and running within two weeks without disrupting operations.”
“More recently, Yousician has also deployed MongoDB Atlas Search for its GuitarTuna product.”
“Yousician can now spin up new clusters in ten minutes, rather than take a couple of days as was previously the case.”
